newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money rises to 10.0/11.0 percent.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money rises to 10.0/11.0 percent.

text.p: Jakarta call money rose to 10.0/11.0 percent from 8.0/9.0 percent on Thursday because of liquidity worries due to month-end factors, dealers said.
They said liquidity was sufficient following early central bank injection of some 880 billion rupiah but the rates rose because of month-end worries.

The central bank offered seven-day central bank certificates (SBIs) at 11.75 percent, 14-day at 12.00 percent, one-month at 12.75 percent, three-month at 13.75 percent, six-month at 14.0 percent and 12-month at 14.5 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Wednesday was 10.50 percent compared with 10.81 percent on Tuesday.
